title: Respondent field spec response
description: Returned by GET /backoffice/assembly/<assembly_id>/respondent-schema.json. Describes an assembly's respondent columns and the valid values for each, so a script outside the app can generate a loadable respondent CSV. Documented in docs/respondent_field_spec.md.

spec_version.description: Bumped when the shape changes in a way a consumer has to notice.

fields.description: The whole field schema, in the order the schema page and the CSV export use: GROUP_DISPLAY_ORDER, then sort_order within each group.

unmatched_target_categories.description: Target categories whose name matches no field_key exactly. Selection pairs a category with a respondent column by exact string match, so these have no column to select on as things stand.

number_to_select.description: How many respondents the selection is to pick. A sensible lower bound on how many rows to generate.

id_column.description: The assembly's configured csv_id_column, else "external_id". Its value becomes Respondent.external_id and must be unique.

columns.description: The header row to write, in order: the id column, then every non-derived field key. Import treats the first column as the id column when none is named, so keeping this order means the file loads either way.

internal_columns_ignored_on_import.description: Export-only columns that import recognises and skips, reporting each once. Present so a generator knows not to emit them; an exported file re-imports cleanly because of them.

field_key.description: The CSV column header, and the Respondent.attributes key (or reserved top-level field name when is_fixed).

label.description: Organiser-facing display label. Not translated - it is typed by the organiser.

is_fixed.description: A reserved top-level Respondent field (email, eligible, can_attend, consent, stay_on_db). Its type and options cannot be edited.

is_derived.description: Computed from other fields, never collected. Excluded from csv.columns.

derived_from.description: Field keys this one is computed from. Null unless is_derived.

derivation_kind.description: How the derivation is done. Empty unless is_derived.

field_type.description: The effective type: for a fixed field the hardcoded FIXED_FIELD_TYPES entry wins over the stored one.

options.description: The permitted values for a choice field. Non-empty for choice_radio and choice_dropdown; null for every other type.

on_registration_page.description: Whether the public registration form collects this field, and how strictly. Governs the form, not CSV import - import accepts any column.

target_values.description: The values and quotas of the TargetCategory whose name equals this field_key. Null when no category matches. These are the values selection will stratify on, so generated data should draw from them.

comment.description: The organiser's free-text note on why these targets were chosen. Empty when none was written.

source_url.description: Where the figures came from, e.g. a census table. Empty when none was given; when set it is a full http:// or https:// address.

value.description: The cell value a respondent must carry to count towards this quota. Compared exactly.

min_flex.description: Selection tolerance below min. Not a constraint on generated data.

max_flex.description: Selection tolerance above max. -1 means unset, and the library calculates a safe default.

percentage_target.description: The share of the committee this value is meant to take, as a percentage. Null when the quota was set as seat counts alone. A better steer for the distribution to generate than min/max, which are rounded to whole seats.

minmax_manual.description: True when an organiser typed min/max by hand, breaking the link to percentage_target. While false, min/max are recalculated from the percentage whenever it or number_to_select changes.

comment.description: The organiser's free-text note on this value. Empty when none was written.
